pr_title: Clean up DNS e2e wrt Jessie/Wheezy
pr_body:
The distinction between Jessie and Wheezy dates back to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/10161 (mid 2015).  For this test, wheezy has long ago been replaced by agnhost.  Now Jessie is gone, too.

/kind cleanup
Fixes  #126936

```release-note
NONE
```

As I said elsewhere, I am not really excited about adding yet another image which will inevitably become out of date.  If we make agnhost build for both debian and alpine, then we could get full coverage on both of the major variants.  I hear Dan's point that we don't need _FULL_ coverage, but these tests are pretty fast, and we could later factor it so that only critical ones run on both.

I'm happy to close this and file a TODO issue instead.  I doubt we'll ever do it unless someone steps up.  This change was attractive because it was easy, but I don't have much time to do it "right", at least not right now.

My opinions:
- The existing code (calling agnhost "wheezy", using an 8-year old distro to represent "modern" behavior) is ridiculous. Given that you already wrote this PR, I'd rank "close this PR and file a TODO" as the worst option (and "merge this PR as-is" as a perfectly acceptable option). If we aren't going to fix any code, we need to at least fix the comments and variable names.
- To the extent that there is benefit in testing multiple libcs, it's mostly because we are worried that _non-glibc_ libcs might behave weirdly (eg, the problem with "`search .`"). But our primary test pod at this point uses agnhost which uses alpine which uses musl, so even if we only test one container here, we are testing non-glibc.

So I vote to merge.

issue_context.title: Public image "jessie-dnsutils" have no update for years
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Public image `registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/jessie-dnsutils:1.3` have no update for years, and it's packed with legacy CoreDNS 1.5.0 inside the docker image.

ref:
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/dns-debugging-resolution/
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/images/jessie-dnsutils/Dockerfile
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commits/master/test/images/jessie-dnsutils (last update was years ago)

### Why is this needed?

`jessie-dnsutils` commonly used for DNS troubleshooting, and it's based on EOL jessie image.
- https://www.debian.org/releases/jessie/
- https://wiki.debian.org/LTS

This is not really a supported image for use beyond testing.  We need to find a better answer for general use.  We do have a k/k/test/images/... dire for it, but obviously Jessies is old.

Wherever possible in the tests we've been moving to the single agnhost utility image, `registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost`, source at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/images/agnhost/README.md

It is actively maintained and supports multi-arch + windows.

While developed for testing, it has already been used in a few of the docs now as a util image for debugging.

For the specific case of:
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/dns-debugging-resolution/

I confirmed this works just as well with `registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.39` as a drop in replacement for the image in that pod.

As a meta point, we should consider if the docs can centrally pick a version so we can easily bump docs references to the latest available tag, since registry.k8s.io doesn't support mutable tags, but we avoid breaking changes in this image.

That is more of a question for https://github.com/kubernetes/website though

I would suggest that we replace references to this image with agnhost, at least as a stopgap.

We should consider if we want to maintain and host an image specifically designed for debugging and what that would look like, but I suspect it winds up being essentially duplicate effort with agnhost anyhow (... though perhaps with a clearer, less "clever" name :-))

the problem I see here is that we are loosing coverage with the libc implementation, right now we have `muslc` and `libc` covered.

We should not completely remove it and instead use one image that has debian or other libc implementation

You're not wrong.  It looks like agnhost is alpine:

```

	/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1 (0x7fa21cb68000)

```

Thast said, if we establish an image just for DNS testing which is libc based, someone has to perpetually build new versions of it.

just replace s/jessie/debian/ for names and s/debian:jessie/debian:stable-slim/ for images
let me do the building of the image first, so you can remove and switch altogether

> we are losing coverage with the libc implementation

Haha, no, we lost the relevant coverage _years_ ago. (But it doesn't matter.)

The timeline here is:
1. Wheezy has a broken DNS implementation which gives ndots-like behavior even if you don't specify ndots. (I think? That's what it seems like from the old discussion.)
2. Kubernetes pre-1.0 assumed that behavior.
3. Jessie fixed that behavior, breaking Kubernetes (#10161).
4. Kubelet was fixed to set `ndots:5` in resolv.conf, fixing Kubernetes under jessie. (#10266)
5. At this time, the e2e test images were all still based on wheezy, so the DNS e2e tests were modified to also test against special jessie-based images (since the wheezy-based tests would have passed with or without the `ndots` fix). It's not clear why it tested against both rather than _only_ testing against jessie, but [Tim commented](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/10266#issuecomment-115103614) "We can reduce the test case back to one when we do a new dnsutils container" so it was clearly intended to be temporary.
6. ... but apparently everyone forgot about that, and mistakenly assumed that the point of the jessie image was that we wanted to test against jessie specifically, rather than that we had just needed something newer than wheezy.

Anyway, while it may happen to be the case that the current version of this test tests two different libcs, that is not the _intent_ of the case (and I don't think there is any reason to believe that libc and musl behave differently here anyway).

If we build agnhost for alpine and debian, I think it would be OK to test both - these tests are fast and cheap, and musl HAS been a problem in the past (not wrt ndots but other things) and we only figured it out when other people reported bugs.

I don't love the idea of having a test image whose sole purpose is DNS, because we are expected to support it (the original bug behind this PR)

> Haha, no, we lost the relevant coverage years ago. (But it doesn't matter.)

@danwinship jessie image is using libc, isn't it?

>  believe that libc and musl behave differently here anyway).

not a lot, but there is precedent https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112135

OK... so, the syntax and semantics of `/etc/resolv.conf` are not sufficiently well defined that we can assume that all software in all containers will interpret it identically. So we need to have an e2e test for "kubelet writes out a resolv.conf that is compatible with the resolver libraries of languages/runtimes we expect people to use in pods". And the easiest way to test that something is interpreting resolv.conf correctly is to just have it resolve things, and the only thing we know for sure that pods will be able to resolve is the Kubernetes DNS stuff. So here we are.

But we don't need to test multiple resolvers in _every_ DNS test. We should split out the alternative-runtime DNS tests into a single separate test case, to make it easier to distinguish "your cluster DNS is broken" failures from "kubelet's resolv.conf generation doesn't work with some languages/runtimes" failures.

And maybe we should test more resolv.conf options, to be able to catch things like #112135?
